articleBody:
Choosing natural marble for your bathroom remodel brings unmatched elegance, but picking the right stone involves more than falling in love with a color swatch. Before you finalize your order, run through this practical checklist to protect your investment.

- [ ] Check stone porosity ratings — High-porosity marble absorbs water, soap, and bath products faster, demanding more frequent sealing.
- [ ] Measure shower floor slope before ordering large format tiles — Large slabs cannot contour to standard center drains without specialized linear drainage systems.
- [ ] Verify slip-resistance ratings on wet surfaces — Honed or textured finishes provide better traction underfoot in showers than high-gloss polished slabs.
- [ ] Inspect slab thickness and batch consistency — Thickness variations between cuts can create uneven transitions and lippage across flat bathroom walls.
- [ ] Order a 10% to 15% waste allowance — Natural veining requires selective cutting and pattern matching around niches and plumbing lines.
- [ ] Confirm adhesive compatibility with your stone supplier — Certain dark mortars can bleed through pale marble and permanently discolor your shower walls.
- [ ] Check edge profiles for exposed corners and curbs — Custom bullnose or mitered edges must be planned before cutting begins to avoid rough edges.
- [ ] Review daily cleaning and maintenance requirements — Acidic bath products etch calcite-based marble, meaning specialty cleaners are essential long-term.

How to use this checklist:
Take this list to your stone supplier and review it with your installer before making final material purchases.
